Interface CharSink

Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface CharSink
A writable destination of characters, such as a text file, that opens a new stream each time it is written.

Unlike a Writer, a sink is not an open resource: it can be kept, passed around and written any number of times, and each write method opens a stream and closes it before returning. Only openStream() and openBufferedStream() leave a stream for the caller to close.

The only abstract method is openStream(), so a lambda makes a sink: 

CharSink sink = () -> new OutputStreamWriter(socket.getOutputStream(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
CharSink.of(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8).writeLines(lines);
Since:
0.1.1

  • Method Details

    • of

      static CharSink of(Path file, OpenOption... options)
      Returns a sink that writes a text file in the current default charset. By default, each write creates the file or replaces its content, but it is not atomic: see AtomicFiles for that.
      Parameters:
      file - the file to write
      options - how to open the file, as for Files.newOutputStream(Path, OpenOption...)
      Returns:
      a sink that writes file
      Since:
      0.1.2
      See Also:
      • of(Path, Charset, OpenOption...)

    • of

      static CharSink of(Path file, Charset charset, OpenOption... options)
      Returns a sink that writes a text file. By default, each write creates the file or replaces its content, but it is not atomic: see AtomicFiles for that.
      Parameters:
      file - the file to write
      charset - the charset to encode the text in
      options - how to open the file, as for Files.newOutputStream(Path, OpenOption...)
      Returns:
      a sink that writes file
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if charset does not support encoding
      See Also:
      • ByteSink.asCharSink(Charset)

    • writeLines

      default void writeLines(Stream<? extends CharSequence> lines) throws IOException
      Writes the lines of a stream to this sink, each followed by the line separator of the system. The stream is consumed but left open. Its lines are checked as they are written, so a null line leaves the lines before it written.
      Parameters:
      lines - the lines to write
      Throws:
      IOException - if this sink cannot be written
      See Also:
      • System.lineSeparator()

    • writeLines

    • asByteSink

      default ByteSink asByteSink()
      Returns a sink that writes bytes to this one, decoded from the current default charset. Writing to it fails with a CharacterCodingException on bytes that are not valid in that charset, rather than replace them. Bytes that end in the middle of a character are reported when the stream is closed.
      Returns:
      a sink of bytes
      Since:
      0.1.2
      See Also:
      • asByteSink(Charset)

    • asByteSink

      default ByteSink asByteSink(Charset charset)
      Returns a sink that writes bytes to this one, decoded from a charset. Writing to it fails with a CharacterCodingException on bytes that are not valid in charset, rather than replace them. Bytes that end in the middle of a character are reported when the stream is closed.
      Parameters:
      charset - the charset the bytes are encoded in
      Returns:
      a sink of bytes
